title: Product of copies of a Noetherian ring is flat Mittag-Leffler
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $A$ be any set. The product module $R^A=\prod_{a\in A}R$, with componentwise $R$-module operations, is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and is a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] to the finite $R$-module $F=R$: it is generated by $1$, including when $R$ is the zero ring. Every ideal is a submodule of $R$, so every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented. Thus $R$ is coherent in the explicit sense required by [lem-trf-coherent-product-flat]. This expands the elementary Noetherian-implies-coherent implication used by the source.

source.place: Tag 05D0 first sentence, expanding Tag 05CY using Tag 00FP(2),(1)

proof.text: Put $M=R^A$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $N\otimes_R R$ with $N$ by $n\otimes r\mapsto rn$, inverse $n\mapsto n\otimes1$. These maps commute with every linear map on $N$, so tensoring any injection with $R$ is injective. Hence each copy of $R$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-trf-coherent-product-flat] to the coherent ring from Step 1 and the constant family $Q_a=R$. It gives flatness of $M$ for arbitrary $A$.

source.place: Tag 05D0 first sentence, Tag 05CZ(1) implies (2), with rank-one flatness written out

proof.text: Let $F$ be finite free, so a finite basis generates it. The leaf [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] implies that every submodule $G\subseteq F$, and $F$ itself, is finitely presented. Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products] with $P=G$ and all factors $Q_\alpha=R$, and with $P=F$ likewise. Composing with the unit maps $G\otimes_R R\cong G$, $F\otimes_R R\cong F$ gives isomorphisms $\eta_G:G\otimes_R M\cong G^A$ and $\eta_F:F\otimes_R M\cong F^A$. Explicitly $\eta_G(g\otimes(r_\alpha)_\alpha)=(r_\alpha g)_\alpha$, and likewise for $F$; these formulas are determined on generators by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For the inclusion $i:G\hookrightarrow F$, both $\eta_F\circ(i\otimes1)$ and the coordinate inclusion composed with $\eta_G$ send $g\otimes(r_\alpha)_\alpha$ to $(r_\alpha i(g))_\alpha$; thus the diagram commutes. In particular these tensor maps are exactly the inclusions $G^A\hookrightarrow F^A$.

source.place: Tag 05D0 diagram, using Tag 00FP for every G and Tag 059K for the product comparisons

proof.text: For $x\in F\otimes_R M$, write $\eta_F(x)=(x_\alpha)_\alpha$ and let $G_0$ be the submodule of all finite $R$-linear combinations of the $x_\alpha$. For every submodule $G\subseteq F$, Step 3 identifies the image of $G\otimes_R M$ with the families in $F^A$ whose every coordinate is in $G$. Thus $x$ is in that image exactly when every $x_\alpha\in G$, exactly when $G_0\subseteq G$. Taking $G=G_0$ also proves that $x$ is in its tensor image. Hence $G_0$ is the least supporting submodule. If $A$ is empty this span is $0$, the family is empty, and the same argument gives least submodule $0$.

source.place: Tag 05D0 final sentence, coordinate-span argument expanded from Step 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-mittag-leffler-criterion] with the module $M$. Step 2 gives its flatness hypothesis, and Steps 3--4 give the least-submodule property for every finite free $F$ and every $x\in F\otimes_R M$. The criterion therefore gives that $M$ is Mittag-Leffler. This and Step 2 are the two conclusions for $R^A$.
